answer: Ridge-terrace violet admission auction: each newcomer seals a violet-stamped bid for a terrace plot on a ridge; the top bid wins at the second price, locking a 60-credit bond. Bids then open; auditors recount violet stamps, and a copied bid burns its bond. 1,000 plots need 1,000 distinct bids: first 40, then 40+6(k-1), so 1,000 fakes cost 3,037,000 vs a 40,000 pool. Rented bids fail: each is key-signed. Honest agents bid 40 and keep it.
